title: The group falls apart and a harsh review
summary: His band went sour and a critic's unfair write-up hurt him deeply.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: I was in San Francisco...and what caused me to arrive in San Francisco is because I had broke the group up. It didn't pan out and all those, everything sort of went sour. But in the meantime, my music didn't. My playing didn't. Personally it didn't. These other things went sour. I didn't have all the recipes to make...to do magic. Things that were happening went kind of sour for me, but my music, to me, personally...I was still satisfied. I liked myself, and what I was doing. I liked myself for the outlook I was having in life. So I had to push on with it, in spite of the...I wasn't going to make readjustment to make that particular thing happen. I had to get with the things that would keep me going forward.

The group broke up and some things just went sour, and I said, 'Well, I've got to keep on doing what I'm doing.' I got a horrible write-up in the newspaper from one of the critics, which I don't care to mention. I thought it was unfair and I think...I don't know why I let something like that affect me, but it really, really affected me. It was very bad, because I felt like...not to just rip up a critic for his opinion, but he could have wrote better if he had spoke to me and see where I

was coming from. There was no way in the world he understood enough to express anything about something I've been living with for twenty years, thirty years. I wasn't able to do it myself, but at least...

Anyhow, I ended up in San Francisco. Little things would tear me up, because I had taken them so serious. But somebody turn around and rip me without even knowing where I was coming from, it really tore me up.
